_synthetic_notice: SYNTHETIC TEACHING FIXTURE. These eight 'papers' are invented for classroom use. Titles, numbers and verdicts are illustrative only and describe no real publication. See README.md.

_vocabulary.note: A degenerate (do-nothing) baseline is a trivial policy whose score any real defence must beat: always-allow admits everything, always-block denies everything, random decides by coin flip, majority-class always predicts the common class.

papers.title: Delimiter quarantine for tool-output injection
papers.defence: wraps untrusted tool output in non-executable delimiters
papers._ground_truth: PASS: beats always-allow (0.71 ASR for doing nothing) and random; base rate and counts present.

papers.title: Instruction hierarchy for agent planning
papers.defence: ranks system over tool instructions by privilege level
papers._ground_truth: FAIL R1+R2+R3: no baseline at all, so nothing rules out a do-nothing policy achieving 0.03; no base rate; no counts.

papers.title: Spotlighting untrusted content in prompts
papers.defence: marks untrusted spans with distinctive formatting
papers._ground_truth: FAIL R1 (lopsided reporting): 'no defence' IS the always-allow policy and it is the FLATTERING baseline (0.68 ASR looks bad, so 0.04 looks good). No unflattering baseline (always-block/random) is reported, so a policy that merely denies more cannot be ruled out.

papers.title: Classifier shield for indirect injection
papers.defence: binary classifier filters tool outputs before planning
papers._ground_truth: FAIL R2: 0.97 accuracy is unknowable without the base rate — if 97% of trials are benign, majority-class (a degenerate policy) also scores 0.97. Majority-class is listed but its score is never reported, so the comparison is decorative.

papers.title: Selective abstention for risky tool calls
papers.defence: abstains whenever a risk score exceeds a threshold
papers._ground_truth: FAIL R4 (degenerate metric): the scoring rule rewards abstention without charging for lost utility, so an always-abstain policy — which does nothing useful — scores equal to a perfect defence. The metric cannot distinguish doing nothing from doing everything.

papers.title: Allowlist mediation for file-system tools
papers.defence: mediates every file operation against an explicit allowlist
papers._ground_truth: PASS: unflattering baselines reported with scores; base rate and counts present.

papers.title: Prompt sandwiching for retrieval agents
papers.defence: repeats the user instruction after retrieved content
papers._ground_truth: INCONCLUSIVE: the right baselines are reported, but n=20 is too small to rule out luck (a coin flip lands within a few points of 0.05 more often than reviewers admit). Underpowered, not wrong.

papers.title: Paraphrasing shield for e-mail agents
papers.defence: paraphrases incoming e-mail before the planner sees it
papers._ground_truth: INCONCLUSIVE: baselines and base rate present, but only rates are reported, never raw counts — the result cannot be recomputed or pooled with other studies.
